import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 242

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/242](https://www.erdosproblems.com/242)
- [Si56] Sierpiński, W., Sur les décompositions de nombres rationnels en fractions primaires.
  Mathesis (1956), 16--32.
-/

open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos242

/--
For every $n>2$ there exist distinct integers $1 ≤ x < y < z$
such that $\frac 4 n = \frac 1 x + \frac 1 y + \frac 1 z$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_242 (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 < n) :
    ∃ x y z : ℕ, 1 ≤ x ∧ x < y ∧ y < z ∧
      (4 / n : ℚ) = 1 / x + 1 / y + 1 / z := by
  sorry

/--
Schinzel conjectured (see [Si56]) the generalisation that, for any fixed $a$, if $n$ is sufficiently
large in terms of $a$ then there exist distinct integers $1\leq x < y < z$ such that
$\frac{a}{n} = \frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{1}{z}.$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_242.variants.schinzel_generalization
    (a : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ x y z : ℕ, 1 ≤ x ∧ x < y ∧ y < z ∧
      (a / n : ℚ) = 1 / x + 1 / y + 1 / z := by
  sorry

end Erdos242

reformulations.difference: Uses eventual quantification over ℕ at Filter.atTop rather than an explicit sufficiently-large threshold depending on a.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each fixed a, Filter.eventually_atTop identifies the statement with ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ x y z satisfying the displayed conditions. The threshold can be increased to max N 1, so allowing zero in the type of n imposes no extra case. Since a is quantified outside the eventual quantifier, N may depend on a, exactly as the source requires. The equivalence with an explicit positive threshold was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean without invoking either conjecture.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/242 — retrieved through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/242, including rendered HTML with the original LaTeX attributes.

C. Pomerance and A. Weingartner, Exceptions to the Erdős–Straus–Schinzel conjecture, arXiv:2511.16817v2, abstract and introduction. Read https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16817 and the LaTeX source from https://arxiv.org/e-print/2511.16817.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Straus_conjecture — formulation, distinct-denominator discussion, generalizations, and references.
Local Mathlib sources: Mathlib/Order/Filter/Defs.lean; Mathlib/Order/Filter/AtTopBot/Defs.lean and Basic.lean; Mathlib/Data/Rat/Defs.lean; Mathlib/Algebra/Field/Rat.lean.
review.notes: Both declarations match the cited problem page, including n > 2 and distinct positive denominators. The research-open tags remain consistent with the sources. Lean checks confirmed rational rather than natural-number division, excluded zero-denominator witnesses, proved the boundary failures at n = 0, 1, 2, constructed witnesses at n = 3, 4, 5, and proved the a = 1 case for every positive n. An exact-rational search verified witnesses for every 3 ≤ n ≤ 100. The full text of [Si56] was not obtainable through its bibliographic links; Schinzel's statement was verified from the explicit problem-page formulation and corroborating modern literature.
